coverage_note: Long English stretches 02:08-05:45 (app talk), 16:32-17:34, 35:00-36:30, 45:21-56:07 (rule discussion, mostly English with Arabic examples). Echo candidates checked: all are real English, no sound-alikes. Engine notes: 07:34 Amal 'سألت' = su2et (سقت, drove; her chat 'ana su2et la-saa3tain'); 33:05 'سوالونا' is most likely وصلونا (he then asks 'Is it وصل'); 08:17/08:49 متهمس/تهمس = mit7ammes with h for 7 (S4). Left out: 12:57 'من أسبوع ماضي' (repeat within 30 s of her fix, GR-28); 10:47 ساعة->ساعات (his own fix); 31:38 واطية->قصيرة (self-fix before her comment); 24:05 هاديين vs هاديات (Amal agreed both work); 38:36 الدرس العربي (Amal: both valid); 59:28 هادي الشنتة (rephrase only, Medi 10-01 ruling); 1:02:30 صديقة/House (help on the way); 1:01:25 يصلوا->يوصلوا (self-fix); 22:25/22:54 صغار->غاليين (self-fix); 53:38 kundara el Chanel (self-fix). Few vocab-B/grammar-B: Amal caught almost every slip in this drill-heavy lesson.

rows.medi_said: I really need the word for motivated.
rows.amal_said: بس a good word for motivation motivated is متشجع.
rows.why: He asked for the word for motivated; she supplied حافز/دافع (motivation) and متشجع (motivated) - a didn't-know.
Right after she taught متشجع he said the verb shape شجّع; she recast متشجع and he repeated it.
He linked متشجع with عشان; she said no, it takes la- and typed 'mitshajje3 + la'.

rows.medi_said: أنا مش، مش، متشجع ... لا إمبارح
rows.why: He was telling about yesterday (إمبارح) with present مش متشجع; she recast it in the past with ما كنت.
He used سويت (I did) / صرت for 'I drove two hours to customers'; she gave su2et (engine wrote سألت, her chat 'ana su2et la-saa3tain') and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: أنا كنت تهَمّس / أنا كنت بحمس / أنا كنت أهمس.
rows.why: He tried verb forms (تهمس / بحمس / أهمس) for 'excited'; she recast the adjective متحمس and he said 'Yeah, that's right'.

rows.medi_said: How do I say customers I was excited for?
rows.amal_said: كنت متحمس إلهم first you have to refer back to them
rows.why: He asked how to say 'excited for (the customers)'; she supplied متحمس إلهم.
Seconds after she gave إلهم he said إنهم (that they) instead of la- + hom; she recast إلهم.

rows.medi_said: Who جيب، جويب. Is it-- It would be جابت؟ بجيب، جابت.
rows.why: For 'I brought' he built جابت (she brought); she gave the I-form جبت and explained the vowel.
11+ takes a singular noun; she said سجادة and he repeated 'cause it's more than ten' (first said at 08:42; one row per brief).

rows.amal_said: No, no, no، بعت. إيش يعني بعت؟
rows.why: She asked if he meant بعت (sold); he repeated it back as بعد (after) and she said no, بعت - a listening slip on her word.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما اشتروا. ما شطار. ما شطار.
rows.amal_said: ما؟ They are a group so they didn't.
rows.why: He settled on ما شطار (singular shape) for the customers; she prompted 'they are a group' and he said ما اشتروا.
A new (unknown) appointment takes no el-; she recast موعد and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: So we say من الأسبوع الماضي.
rows.why: He left out the preposition for 'since last week'; she said 'So we say من الأسبوع الماضي'.

rows.medi_said: كانت متحمسة كتير لما شفت السجادة.
rows.amal_said: شافت. ... So I showed is a different verb.
rows.why: He meant 'when I showed her the rug' but said شفت (I saw); she told him 'I showed is a different verb' and he moved to فرجيت.
rows.english: when I showed her the rug

rows.why: Showed HER needs the object ending on the verb; she recast with the ending and confirmed فرجتها.

rows.amal_said: young children are خلاص one label. So، الولاد الصغار.
rows.why: Noun + adjective in a general statement: both take el-; she recast الولاد الصغار.
For 'are fun' he used بيضحكوا (they laugh / are funny); she flagged it and he switched to بيبسطوا, then بيسلوا.

rows.medi_said: هدول فساتين، الـ uh, الصغار الـ، uh, الـ غا-غاليين.
rows.amal_said: Where do I put the L?
rows.why: The noun after هدول keeps el-; she asked where the L goes and he fixed it to هدول الفساتين.
He said the singular 'the long trip'; she repeated 'Long trips' (English prompt) and he changed to the plural سفرات ... طوال.

rows.medi_said: So, هناك is that, right? ... And then هناك is that?
rows.amal_said: No, hunak is not in this list. Hunak means over there.
rows.chat: haada, haadi, hadak, hadik, hadol, hadolak
rows.why: He used هناك (over there) for 'that'; she said no, hunak means over there and is not a demonstrative.

rows.medi_said: That guy. So, هداك الـ زلمة؟
rows.why: Her prompt was 'that guy, meaning young'; he said زلمة (man), she repeated 'young guy, young man' and he said الشاب.
عيلة is one feminine noun, so هادي not هدول; she repeated 'This family' and he fixed it.
For 'visited us' he said (engine wrote سوالونا, likely وصلونا - he then asks about وصل); she said no, it means arrive/reach, and he found زارونا.
'A big table' takes no el- on the adjective; she asked if L is needed and he said طاولة كبيرة.
He said مفتاح (key) for 'open'; she recast مفتوح.
باب is masculine so the adjective is مفتوح; she recast and he said 'cause it's bab'.

rows.medi_said: So el ba-- No. Yeah, el bab.
rows.why: First word of an idafa never takes el-; she said 'No ال' and he built باب الغرفة المفتوح.

rows.medi_said: is sick. Uh, oh my God. Uh, uh, awahi, awa-- ... I forgot the word for, like, mild sickness.
rows.why: He said he forgot the word for sick; she supplied عيانة - a didn't-know.

rows.amal_said: So where, where do I put the ال؟ ... No. ... It's the sick boy.
rows.chat: el-walad el-3ayaan laazem ydall fi beito
rows.why: 'The sick boy' needs el- on both noun and adjective; she asked where the L goes, said no to 'walad al ayan', and he fixed it to الولد العيان.
After لازم the verb drops b-; she repeated لازم and he said 'needs to say يضل'.
Stay IN his home takes في not على; she rephrased in English 'In his home' and he said في بيته.

rows.amal_said: ممتاز. So for feminine nouns, what do we add?
rows.why: Feminine first word of an idafa grows -t; right after his answer she asked what we add to feminine nouns, he said the T, and her chat wrote sayyaaret.

rows.amal_said: I'm not describing the tree. I'm saying it's the tree of apples. ... It's a dufa still. ... هذه شجرة التفاح.
rows.why: He treated 'the apple tree' as noun + adjective (el- on both); she said it is idafa (tree of apples) and later gave شجرة التفاح.

rows.amal_said: ليش فيه هون؟ ... No, they're just هون. طلاب الجامعة هون.
rows.why: He used فيه (there is) for 'are'; she asked why, said they're just هون - no word for 'are'.

rows.amal_said: What's bag؟ Uh, the other word ... شنتة سفر.
rows.why: For 'suitcase' he offered جزدان (purse/wallet); she asked for the other word, he said he forgot, and she gave شنتة سفر.

rows.medi_said: So after هذي and هدول and هناك and,
rows.why: Again listed هناك among the demonstratives; she asked 'هناك is what?' and he fixed it to هذيك and هذاك (same slip as 27:04, a new moment 37 min later).
